title: Power Input Measurements in Stirred Bioreactors at Laboratory Scale
protocol: Fill a Duran glass bottle with water and sucrose of different concentrations (20 - 60 %w/w).
Mix the content with a magnetic stirrer until the sucrose has completely dissolved.
For sucrose concentrations in excess of 40 %w/w, add the sucrose intermittently and heat the glass bottle slightly (~50 °C).
Let the sucrose solution cool down to room temperature before use.
After starting the software, initiate communication with the control unit by selecting the correct serial COM port from the dropdown menu and clicking the Connect button.
Set up the data file path inside the bioreactor control unit software in order to store the data on the operator PC.
Open the Settings tab page and hit the folder symbol next to the Data file location text field.
In the file dialog window, browse to the desired folder, type a file name into the File name text field, and click the OK button.
Set up a routine inside the recipe manager of the bioreactor control unit software.
Open the Recipe tab page and type input values for phase elapsed time (min) and impeller speed (rpm).
The profile is automatically displayed in the chart.
Increase agitator speed stepwise from 100 rpm to 300 rpm, maintaining each value for 4 minutes.
Adjust minimum and maximum speeds according to torque sensor resolution and nominal torque.
Avoid vortex formation by selecting appropriate speed ranges.
Select a file path and type a file name to save the recipe.
Hit the OK button to save the file.
Install the torque transducer in a specially designed holder using screws.
Fix the sensor into place with screws in the holder that incorporates an air bearing.
Mount the brushless servo agitator motor onto the top of the holder.
Fix the torque transducer to the vertical holder mounting using four screws.
Connect the motor shaft to the drive shaft of the torque transducer using a metal bellow coupling and tighten the coupling using screws.
Connect the agitator shaft to the measurement shaft of the torque transducer using another metal bellow coupling.
Mount the sensor holder onto the bioreactor head plate.
Install the impellers on the agitator shaft with the desired off-bottom clearance.
Mount baffles inside the bioreactor if required.
Install additional installations (e.g., sampling and harvest tubes, electrochemical sensors) inside the bioreactor if required.
Install the desired bioreactor in the vessel holder if required.
Place the head plate onto the bioreactor tank for investigations of single-use bioreactors and tighten with screws.
Disassemble the top mounted tubing ports from the plastic head plates using appropriate cutting tools for investigations of single-use bioreactors.
Place the plastic vessel into the holder for investigations of single-use bioreactors.
Place a temperature sensor inside the bioreactor and connect it to the control unit.
Connect the tubing for the pressurized air to the gas inlet port of the air bearing.
Apply a pressure of around 5.5 bar provided by a compressor.
Connect the torque transducer to the A/D converter.
Power on the transmitter.
Open the software for the data acquisition of torque sensor signal.
Configure the measurement preferences in the DAQ channels window.
Initialize and activate the first two channels in the DAQ channels window.
Set the torque signal on channel 0.
Set the rotational speed signal on channel 1.
Click the Live update button to display the current measurement values.
Zero balance the torque channel if the absolute torque signal without rotation is larger than 0.1 mN·m.
Navigate to the DAQ job tab page and define a data acquisition rate of 2 Hz from the dropdown menu list.
Set the Start option to Immediately at job start.
Set the Stop option to Duration from the dropdown lists.
Define a time span for the Sample duration that is longer than the time required to finish the measurement.
Navigate to the Data storage settings page.
Select the option ASCII + channel info from the dropdown list to set the File format for the data save file.
Set a file path on the PC hard drive for the measurement Output file.
Click the Start button on the DAQ job menu page in the control and data acquisition software for the torque meter.
Start the data acquisition for the agitator speed and temperature in the bioreactor control unit software by clicking the DAQ start button on the Settings tab page.
Start the agitator control in the control unit software with a manual set-point or the pre-defined recipe scheme.
Type the desired set-point into the text box and click on the ‘Agitator control on’ item if conducting a single measurement.
Navigate to the Phases tab page and click the Start button if multiple measurements with a recipe are conducted.
Click the Save data now button in the data acquisition software to save the data for each measurement.
Repeat the measurement for each desired agitator speed without liquid inside the bioreactor vessel.
Pour water (or the sucrose solution) through a funnel into the bioreactor.
Ensure that the liquid completely covers the impellers.
Measure torque values in the empty vessel to determine residual friction losses.
Subtract the measured dead torque from values determined in the liquid.
Average the torque values for each agitator speed after achieving a quasi-stable signal.
Calculate the mean value over at least 2 minutes for each condition.
Use Matlab code to process raw data and calculate phase average rotational speed, Reynolds number, and torque values.
Import the raw data file from the data recording using the provided script.
Visualize outcomes of the processed data.
Store results in a second text file for further processing.
Subtract the torque values obtained in the empty vessel from those measured in the liquid to obtain the effective torque values.
Calculate the power input and dimensionless power number from the time-averaged torque values according to Eq. 1 and Eq. 2.
